initial.name: bash
initial.description:
Run commands in a bash shell
* When invoking this tool, the contents of the "command" parameter does NOT need to be XML-escaped.
* You don't have access to the internet via this tool.
* You do have access to a mirror of common linux and python packages via apt and pip.
* State is persistent across command calls and discussions with the user.
* To inspect a particular line range of a file, e.g. lines 10-25, try 'sed -n 10,25p /path/to/the/file'.
* Please avoid commands that may produce a very large amount of output.
* Please run long lived commands in the background, e.g. 'sleep 10 &' or start a server in the background.

command.description: The bash command to run. Relative path is preferred in the command.

initial.name: create_worktree
initial.description: Create a git worktree on a new branch and move this session into it. Use it when a task needs its own checkout: work in parallel with another agent on the same repository, try a change without touching the main working tree, or leave a build in place while starting something else. The new checkout is created from HEAD, or from the revision you name; uncommitted changes in the current checkout do not carry over. Every later file, shell, and search call resolves against it, and file writes are confined to it. Subagents already get their own worktree automatically.

name.description: Worktree name: letters, digits, dots, dashes, or underscores. The branch and the checkout directory both use it. Omit for a generated name.

from.description: Revision the new branch starts from: a branch, tag, or commit. Defaults to HEAD of the session's repository.

initial.name: git_branch
initial.description: List, create, switch, or delete branches. Switching refuses while the checkout has uncommitted changes unless allow_dirty is true, because a switch would otherwise carry or block them unpredictably. Deleting refuses an unmerged branch unless force is true.

operation.description: What to do: list every local branch, switch to one, create one, or delete one.

name.description: Branch name; required for switch, create, and delete.

from.description: Revision a created branch starts from. Defaults to HEAD.

allow_dirty.description: Switch even though the checkout has uncommitted changes.

force.description: Delete a branch that is not merged.

initial.name: git_commit
initial.description: Record the staged changes as a commit. Pass paths to stage those paths first, or omit them to commit exactly what the index holds. The message goes to git verbatim, so keep it to one clear subject line and, when useful, a body after a blank line.

message.description: Commit message, passed to git verbatim.

paths.description: Repository-relative paths to stage before committing; omit to commit the index as it stands.

initial.name: git_diff
initial.description: Show a unified diff of this session's repository. By default it compares the working tree with the index, so it shows what is not staged yet; use staged to compare the index with HEAD, or range for two revisions such as "main..HEAD". A long diff is cut and marked truncated.

path.description: Repository-relative path to diff; omit for the whole checkout.

staged.description: Compare the index with HEAD instead of the working tree with the index.

range.description: Two revisions to compare, such as "main..HEAD". Takes precedence over staged.

initial.name: git_log
initial.description: List recent commits in this session's repository, newest first, with hash, author, date, and subject. Use it to see what landed before changing history or writing a commit message.

limit.description: How many commits to report. Omit for the configured default.

initial.name: git_merge
initial.description: Merge a branch or revision into the checked-out branch. A merge that conflicts returns the paths left with conflicts instead of raising only an exit status; abort discards an in-progress merge.

ref.description: Branch or revision to merge into the checked-out branch.

abort.description: Abort an in-progress merge instead of starting one.

initial.name: git_remote
initial.description: Fetch from a remote or push the current branch to it. Omit remote to use the branch's own remote and omit branch to push the branch that is checked out. The command's own output is returned.

operation.description: Fetch remote updates, or push the current branch.

remote.description: Remote name; omit to use the branch's own remote.

branch.description: Branch to push; omit to push the checked-out branch.

initial.name: git_status
initial.description: Report the repository this session works in: checked-out branch, upstream and commits ahead or behind it, and every changed path with its staged and unstaged change. Start here before committing or switching branches.

initial.name: read_aloud
initial.description: Turn spoken read-aloud of your replies on or off for this session. Switch it on when the user wants to hear the answers — language practice, pronunciation, or a hands-free conversation — and off when they ask you to stop. It changes only the reader; your replies themselves stay text.

enabled.description: true to read your replies aloud from now on, false to stop reading them.

initial.name: remove_worktree
initial.description: Remove a git worktree created by create_worktree or for a subagent, once its branch is merged or no longer needed. Without a name, removes the worktree this session works in and moves the session back to the repository's main checkout. Fails while the worktree has uncommitted changes. With delete_branch, also deletes its branch, which git refuses while the branch is unmerged.

name.description: Name of the worktree to remove, as its directory and branch name it (without the branch prefix). Omit to remove the worktree this session works in.

delete_branch.description: Also delete the worktree's branch. Git refuses while the branch is not merged.

initial.name: str_replace_editor
initial.description:
Custom editing tool for viewing, creating and editing files
* State is persistent across command calls and discussions with the user
* If `path` is a file, `view` displays the result of applying `cat -n`. If `path` is a directory, `view` lists non-hidden files and directories up to 2 levels deep
* The `create` command cannot be used if the specified `path` already exists as a file
* If a `command` generates a long output, it will be truncated and marked with `<response clipped>`
* A null placeholder for a parameter unused by the selected command is treated as omitted. Required parameters still need values; omit `str_replace.new_str` rather than setting it to null when deleting a match

Notes for using the `str_replace` command:
* The `old_str` parameter should match EXACTLY one or more consecutive lines from the original file. Be mindful of whitespaces!
* If the `old_str` parameter is not unique in the file, the replacement will not be performed. Make sure to include enough context in `old_str` to make it unique
* The `new_str` parameter should contain the edited lines that should replace the `old_str`

command.description: The commands to run. Allowed options are: `view`, `create`, `str_replace`, `insert`.

path.description: Absolute path to file or directory, e.g. `/repo/file.py` or `/repo`.

file_text.description: Required string parameter of `create` command, with the content of the file to be created. A null placeholder is treated as omitted by commands that do not use this parameter.

insert_line.description: Required integer parameter of `insert` command. The `new_str` will be inserted AFTER the line `insert_line` of `path`. A null placeholder is treated as omitted by commands that do not use this parameter.

new_str.description: Optional string parameter of `str_replace` command containing the new string (if omitted, no string will be added). Required string parameter of `insert` command containing the string to insert. A null placeholder is accepted only by commands that do not use this parameter.

old_str.description: Required string parameter of `str_replace` command containing the string in `path` to replace. A null placeholder is treated as omitted by commands that do not use this parameter.

view_range.description: Optional parameter of `view` command when `path` points to a file. If omitted or null, the full file is shown. If provided, the file will be shown in the indicated line number range, e.g. [11, 12] will show lines 11 and 12. Indexing at 1 to start. Setting `[start_line, -1]` shows all lines from `start_line` to the end of the file.

initial.name: working_directory
initial.description: Read or change this session's working directory. With no path, report the current directory. With a path, resolve it (absolute, or relative to the current directory), require an existing directory, and make it the directory every later file, shell, and search call resolves against. The change lasts for the rest of the session; there is no directory stack to pop.

path.description: Directory to enter: absolute, or relative to the current working directory. Omit to read the current directory.
